cowboy noun

classical

Verg. G. 3.344

armentārius, armentāriī m.

noun, second declension

herdsman of cattle

The man who drives the herds (armenta) of cattle and horses; Lewis & Short sets him apart from the bubulcus, who ploughs with oxen.

Other words

  • bubulcus Americānus — cowboy

    also used · modern · Traupman 298

    Classically a bubulcus is a ploughman with his oxen; Lewis & Short finds the sense “herdsman” only after Augustus, in the Digest.

Examples

  • omnia sēcum armentārius Āfer agit

    the African herdsman takes everything with him (as he roams the desert with his herd)Verg. G. 3.343–344

See also shepherd, farmer.

SourcesLewis & Short: armentarius · Lewis & Short: bubulcus
